source_review.notes: Checked all ten references. Current Java SE 26 BlockingQueue operation families, bounded-capacity, bulk, close absence, and memory effects; Python 3.14.7 MPMC, approximate inspection, task tracking, and shutdown behavior; Rust 1.98 mpsc channel variants; and current Go channel and memory-model rules were verified against official specifications.

evidence: Reviewed abstract sequence Q, capacity K, lifecycle L, accepted A, in-flight F, terminal T, ring indices/count, linearization intervals, and queueing quantities.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Representation, ownership, linearizability, progress, capacity, and workload claims are consistently separated.

evidence: Executed all 20 order-preserving schedules of three puts and three takes and independently confirmed 4 capacity-two-safe, 15 underflow, and 1 overflow histories.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Counts match exact stdout and the finite abstract occupancy model.

evidence: Re-derived sequence/ring enqueue and dequeue preservation, close/drain transitions, accepted-buffered-in-flight-terminal reconciliation, and real-time linearization constraints.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The proof explicitly excludes unstated FIFO implementation, fairness, visibility, completion, durability, and reclamation claims.

evidence: Reviewed empty/full, wraparound, immediate/timed/blocking races, close with both waiter classes, drain/abort, duplicate completion, recursive submission, large payloads, mutable aliases, bulk partial effects, priority starvation, async blocking, and destruction.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Every enqueue outcome preserves exactly one item owner and every accepted item receives a terminal disposition.

evidence: Checked capacity, sequence/ring correspondence, unique representation, ownership transfer, FIFO scope, predicate-loop protection, item/byte/waiter bounds, lifecycle wakeup, terminal reconciliation, and safe reclamation obligations.
invariant_checking.notes: Transient empty, closed-drained, dequeue, and processing completion remain distinct states.

evidence: Reviewed bounded-transition induction, overlapping-enqueue linearization, recursive-submission deadlock, poison-pill counterexample, and the SPSC-to-MPMC proof boundary.
proof_review.notes: Safety, progress, overload, lifecycle, and failure-domain properties are not conflated.

evidence: Audited the monitor schema, ring derivation, linearizability discussion, lock-free and reclamation claims, API comparisons, and safety-critical boundary.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The monitor schema is explicitly non-executable and current API claims remain version-scoped.

evidence: Reproduced one executable Python result and confirmed one schematic fence is intentionally skipped with a stated reason.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Evidence disclaims stored values, real threads, FIFO implementation, wakeups, close, cancellation, weak memory, fairness, reclamation, and arbitrary queue correctness.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed distinctions among topology, abstract order, representation, linearization, ownership, backpressure, overload, close, drain, abort, processing completion, progress, and reclamation.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed worker pools, slot/byte/waiter bounds, immediate/timed/blocking policy, cancellation, close-and-wake, poison pills, recursive submission, metrics, async queues, durable brokers, overload, tests, and shutdown.

pedagogical_review.notes: The chapter develops queue correctness from abstract state and ownership through production overload and lifecycle using ten distinct examples and five progressively demanding matched exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, practitioner, railway, medical-device, clinical, real-time, controls, hardware, functional-safety, cybersecurity, regulatory, quality, or human-factors review is claimed. Finite enumeration, source checking, and manual analysis do not prove a production queue implementation, fairness, timing, durability, distributed delivery, or safety-critical deployment fitness.
